### 1. Exact Idempotency Protocol for Stripe Webhooks

Stripe guarantees **at-least-once delivery**. A robust idempotency protocol must decouple the transport-level acknowledgment from domain-level side effects using a multi-phase verification, deduplication, and atomic state-transition lifecycle.

invariantResults.text: Idempotency record must be stored atomically within the same database transaction as the state mutation (or via outbox)
Identifies Redis-only deduplication failure modes (cache eviction, unpersisted writes, race window)
Handles concurrent in-flight duplicates via unique constraint violation with proper retry or 409/200 response
Distinguishes between retryable transient failure and terminal duplicate replay

trapResults.text: Storing idempotency key in Redis without database transactional synchronization
Returning HTTP 500 on duplicate webhook instead of HTTP 200 acknowledging receipt
Fulfilling order before durable commit of event processing record

outputSnippet:

### 1. Step-by-Step Zero-Downtime Migration Plan (Expand-and-Contract)

This migration uses the **Expand-and-Contract (Parallel Run)** pattern to process 50,000,000 rows under active load (5,000 read QPS, 500 write QPS) without locking out concurrent transactions or exceeding connection pool ca

invariantResults.text: Prohibits single-statement table-wide UPDATE due to table bloat, lock contention, and transaction replication lag

Uses phased expand-and-contract: 1) add nullable columns; 2) dual-write (trigger or app code); 3) batch backfill with bounded chunk sizes (e.g. 1000-5000 rows by primary key); 4) enforce NOT NULL constraint via CHECK ... NOT VALID followed by VALIDATE CONSTRAINT; 5) switch reads; 6) remove dual-write; 7) drop old column
Defines explicit non-destructive rollback path at every phase
Identifies AccessExclusiveLock required for ALTER TABLE DROP COLUMN and schedules during low traffic or with low lock_timeout

trapResults.text: Proposing single massive UPDATE statement
Adding NOT NULL column without default in older Postgres or locking table
Dropping old column before all application replicas are running new code

name: Hierarchical Authorization & Privilege Escalation Boundary Analysis
outputSnippet:
### 1. Privilege Escalation Vectors

If `editUserRole(targetUserId, newRole)` asserts only that the invoking user holds `user:edit_role`, the authorization boundary fails to evaluate the relationship between the actor, the target, the assigned role, and the organizational boundary. This enables the

invariantResults.text: Vertical escalation: Caller cannot grant a role equal to or higher than their own hierarchy level (Admin cannot assign Owner)
Self-escalation / target hierarchy: Caller cannot edit roles of users who possess equal or higher hierarchy (Admin cannot demote or modify Owner)
Cross-tenant IDOR: Must assert targetUserId belongs to the exact same organization_id as the authenticated context
Immediate session invalidation / token versioning upon role change to prevent stale privilege persistence
Fail-closed evaluation default

trapResults.text: Only checking permission string without hierarchy and target-user ownership validation
Allowing Admin to assign Owner role
Ignoring cross-tenant target validation
